body.text: Overview and Empirical Foundations of Economy of East Africa

The economy of East Africa is a diverse and rapidly developing regional economy, with agriculture playing a pivotal role as a backbone of the economy. As of 2026, East Africa has a GDP of around US$575.83 billion (nominal) and US$1.935 trillion (PPP) accounting for approximately 18% of Africa's total GDP. The region has an average growth rate of 5.9%, making it the fastest-growing region in Africa and placing it among the continent's strongest-performing regions.Kenya and Ethiopia are the largest national economies, together contributing roughly 48% of the regional economy. Nairobi and Addis Ababa are the main economic hubs, while other major economic centres include Dar es Salaam, Kampala, Mombasa, and Kigali.

As of 2026, East Africa’s economies varied significantly in size and wealth with the region having both the most wealthiest countries and most poorest countries in Africa. Kenya was the largest state economy, with a GDP of $151 billion, followed by Ethiopia at $127 billion and Tanzania at $96 billion.
